content.user_title: Debug Code Failures with Root Cause Analysis
content.value_statement: Software defects can hide behind unclear errors and failing tests. This skill guides structured diagnosis, minimal fixes, verification, and prevention.
actual_capabilities: Captures error messages, stack traces, and reproduction steps before proposing fixes.
Guides isolation of the failing location through logs, recent changes, and hypotheses.
Recommends minimal code fixes focused on the underlying defect.
Defines verification steps to confirm the issue is resolved.
Suggests prevention actions after the root cause is understood.
limitations: It does not execute tests or inspect repositories without tool access from the host agent.
It depends on accurate error messages, logs, and reproduction details from the user.
It cannot guarantee a fix when the failure is intermittent or environment-specific.
It is not a replacement for security review, performance profiling, or production incident response.

use_cases.title: Resolve Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Diagnose test output, isolate the failing behavior, and propose a minimal correction with verification steps.

use_cases.title: Investigate Runtime Errors
use_cases.description: Turn stack traces and logs into a clear root cause, fix plan, and prevention recommendation.

use_cases.title: Triage Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare recent changes against unexpected behavior and build a focused hypothesis list.

prompt_templates.title: Explain This Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner debugging with a visible error message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug this error. I will provide the error message, stack trace, expected behavior, actual behavior, and the steps I used to reproduce it.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Failing Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused diagnosis for a single failing test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this failing test. Identify the likely root cause, the smallest fix, and the exact verification steps I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Regression
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation after recent code changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug this regression. Compare the recent changes with the new behavior, rank likely causes, and propose targeted checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Debugging Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation for unclear or intermittent failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structured debugging plan for this intermittent issue. Include hypotheses, evidence to collect, isolation steps, fix strategy, and prevention recommendations.

output_examples.input: A unit test fails after a refactor, but the application still starts normally.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate test setup issues from application behavior, inspect recent changes, identify the likely broken assumption, and recommend a minimal verification path.

output_examples.input: A production error includes a stack trace, but the user cannot reproduce it locally.
output_examples.output: The skill would extract the failure location, list missing context, form ranked hypotheses, and suggest logs or checks that narrow the cause.

output_examples.input: A feature behaves differently after a dependency update.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare expected and actual behavior, focus on changed dependency behavior, and propose checks before recommending a fix.

best_practices: Provide the exact error message, stack trace, and reproduction steps before asking for a fix.
Verify each hypothesis with targeted evidence before changing several areas at once.
Run the smallest meaningful test after each fix, then add prevention coverage.
anti_patterns: Asking for broad rewrites before identifying the failing behavior.
Sharing only a vague symptom without logs, inputs, or expected behavior.
Skipping verification after a change appears to remove the visible error.

faq.question: What kinds of bugs is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for errors, failing tests, regressions, and unexpected behavior with observable evidence.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend tests, but execution depends on the host agent and available tools.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the error message, stack trace, reproduction steps, expected behavior, and recent changes.

faq.question: Can it debug intermittent issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can build a hypothesis-driven plan, but intermittent failures may require more logs and repeated checks.

faq.question: Will it always produce a code fix?
faq.answer: No. It first seeks the root cause, then recommends a minimal fix when evidence supports one.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to one programming language?
faq.answer: No. The process is language-agnostic and can be applied to many software debugging tasks.
